answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, epoch-long bond before it earns task fees; if linked identities repeat fraudulent claims, a random audit slashes the bond, making every fake account a capital cost rather than a free copy. An audit trail can anchor claims to a jetty, meadow, and oasis of independent task contexts, so fabricated identities must risk separate deposits across unrelated work. An attacker pays both the opportunity cost of locked funds and the expected loss from detection, while honest agents recover their bond.
